B_source.statement:
Let $t \in \R$ be a [[Definition:Real Number|real number]].
Then:
:$t^2 \ge 0$

validity_conditions: For a,b >= 0 the real square roots exist, so t = sqrt(a) - sqrt(b) is real.
t^2 >= 0 expands to a - 2 sqrt(ab) + b >= 0.
proof_plan:
Let $t = \sqrt a - \sqrt b$.
As $a, b \ge 0$, the [[Definition:Square Root|square roots]] exist and $t \in \R$.

From [[Square of Real Number is Non-Negative]]:
:$\paren {\sqrt a - \sqrt b}^2 \ge 0$
